title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs. Hearings held.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 requires companies that develop or deploy AI systems to assess and disclose the potential risks associated with their technology, such as safety, bias, and privacy impacts. It establishes a federal oversight body that reviews these risk reports and can impose penalties or mandate mitigation measures to protect the public.

title: To establish in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency of the Department of Homeland Security a task force on artificial intelligence, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy establishes a new task force within the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) of the Department of Homeland Security to focus on artificial intelligence matters. The task force will address AI‑related concerns and support other related initiatives as needed.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed federal law that aims to regulate the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems in the United States. It establishes safety standards, transparency requirements, and enforcement mechanisms to protect consumers, workers, and the public from potential harms caused by advanced AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on the construction of new AI data centers to address environmental and regulatory concerns. The bill aims to ensure responsible development of AI infrastructure while giving time to establish standards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 seeks to establish rules that limit the environmental damage caused by AI technologies, such as energy consumption and e‑waste. It requires companies to measure, report, and reduce the carbon footprint of their AI systems and to invest in greener hardware and software solutions.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 establishes that human physicians must remain the primary providers of medical care, preventing artificial intelligence from replacing doctors in diagnosis, treatment planning, or patient interactions. It imposes strict regulatory limits on AI medical tools, requiring mandatory human oversight, transparency, and accountability to ensure patient safety and uphold medical professionalism.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is aimed at ensuring that artificial‑intelligence technologies are developed and deployed in ways that benefit the U.S. economy and its citizens, emphasizing job creation, innovation, and national security. The bill also proposes funding for AI research, workforce training programs, and safeguards to protect privacy and civil liberties while encouraging responsible use of AI.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 is a proposed law aimed at integrating AI education into U.S. K–12 schools. It seeks to ensure that students, teachers, and schools are equipped with the knowledge and resources needed to safely and effectively use AI technologies.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 is a U.S. law that requires developers and researchers to prioritize safety, transparency, and accountability in AI systems. It sets standards and oversight mechanisms so that new AI technologies are tested for reliability, biases are addressed, and the public is kept informed about potential risks.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025 is a law designed to improve the safety, reliability, and accountability of AI systems by establishing clear standards and oversight for AI research. It also encourages responsible innovation and ensures that AI products are rigorously tested before deployment.

title: To direct the Secretary of Homeland Security, acting through the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a Critical Infrastructure AI Cyber Defense Pilot Program, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The policy directs the Secretary of Homeland Security—via the Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency—to launch a pilot program that uses AI to strengthen cyber defenses for critical infrastructure. It also includes other related measures, though those details are not specified.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 sets out rules and standards for teaching artificial intelligence concepts to students from kindergarten through 12th grade. It also requires schools and educators to develop and maintain programs that prepare both students and staff for the growing role of AI in everyday life and future careers.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act is proposed legislation that sets out rules for how artificial intelligence can be used in reviewing and deciding veterans’ benefits claims. It seeks to make AI decision‑making transparent, fair, and subject to oversight so that veterans are treated justly.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 is designed to make AI systems used in Virginia more open and understandable by requiring developers and operators to disclose how the AI works, what data it uses, and how it makes decisions. It also mandates that companies provide clear, consumer-friendly explanations of any AI-driven outcomes so people can see how and why decisions affecting them were made.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a national program to raise public understanding of artificial intelligence. It funds educational initiatives and public outreach to help people recognize both the benefits and risks of AI.

title: A resolution establishing the Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence.
action: Referred to the Committee on Rules and Administration. (text: CR S5172-5174)
summary: The resolution creates a new Select Committee dedicated to addressing issues related to artificial intelligence. This committee will examine AI's impact, propose policies, and recommend actions to ensure the technology benefits society responsibly.

title: A bill to provide for the retraining and support of workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence, to require Federal action during periods of elevated unemployment, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: This bill proposes federal programs to retrain and support workers displaced by automation technologies or artificial intelligence. It also requires the government to act during periods of elevated unemployment and includes additional related measures.

title: A resolution expressing the sense of the Senate regarding the importance of religious freedom, authoritative texts, and transparency in artificial intelligence systems.
action: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S4958; text: CR S4951)
summary: The Senate resolution stresses that protecting religious freedom must be a priority as artificial intelligence systems grow in influence. It also urges that AI be built and operated with clear, authoritative guidelines and transparent processes to promote fairness and accountability.

title: A bill to establish the Artificial Intelligence Safety Board, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The bill proposes creating an Artificial Intelligence Safety Board to oversee the development and deployment of AI technologies, ensuring they meet safety standards and protect public welfare. It also includes additional measures—such as oversight requirements, reporting mandates, and potential funding—to support AI governance and related policy initiatives.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a policy aimed at ensuring AI technologies do not mislead or deceive consumers. It sets standards for transparency and accountability so users can trust the information provided by AI systems.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to submit a report to Congress on how artificial intelligence systems are used under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. The report will cover AI’s role in acquiring, analyzing, querying, disseminating, and otherwise accessing relevant information.

title: Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce, and in addition to the Committees on Science, Space, and Technology, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This act seeks to enhance AI education and bolster workforce readiness for AI‑driven industries. It proposes funding initiatives, curriculum guidelines, and training programs to equip individuals with relevant AI skills.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 26 - 21.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act is legislation that encourages the development and use of open‑source artificial intelligence, aiming to keep AI tools accessible, transparent, and widely available. It proposes funding, incentives, and a regulatory framework to promote collaboration, innovation, and responsible use of AI within an open‑source ecosystem.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a proposed law that aims to prevent businesses from using artificial‑intelligence tools to inflate prices or manipulate wages in ways that harm consumers and workers. It would set up regulatory oversight, enforcement mechanisms, and penalties to ensure that AI technologies are used fairly in pricing and employment practices.

title: A bill to establish the Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill proposes creating a Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations to oversee and investigate incidents related to AI and cybersecurity. The bill also includes additional provisions aimed at strengthening national security and regulatory compliance.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act requires that developers of artificial intelligence systems disclose the inner workings, training data, and decision‑making logic of their models so that users can understand how the AI makes predictions. It aims to increase transparency, accountability, and public trust in AI applications by mandating that model details be publicly available and easily understandable.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act seeks to shield households from rising utility bills caused by the growing power demands of AI data centers. It proposes measures such as energy cost caps, tax incentives for renewable energy use, and transparency requirements for data center operators.

title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: This act creates a government department focused on overseeing the development and use of advanced technology and artificial intelligence. It aims to promote innovation while ensuring that AI research, industry practices, and public policies are safe, ethical, and accountable.
